title: Minimum Time For K Virus Variants to Spread
summary: Given n unique virus variants on an infinite 2D grid, where each variant starts at a point given by a 2D array, determine the minimum number of days required for any point to have at least k different virus variants, with each variant spreading to adjacent cells daily.
statement: Given n unique virus variants on an infinite 2D grid, where each variant starts at a point given by a 2D array, determine the minimum number of days required for any point to have at least k different virus variants, with each variant spreading to adjacent cells daily.
constraints: points contains 2 through 50 unique integer coordinates with each x,y from 1 through 100.
Each variant spreads one Manhattan-distance step per day; find the first day some integer grid point has at least k variants.
hints: The transform u=x+y, v=x-y turns each Manhattan diamond into an axis-aligned square, with valid grid points requiring u and v to share parity.
Binary-search days. At each square u-boundary, gather covering v-intervals and test same-parity endpoints for overlap by at least k intervals.
Transform centers; feasible(t) checks boundary u values and parity-adjusted interval starts; lower-bound search the first feasible t.

Any k-square intersection contains a boundary coordinate of one participating square, and its v intersection contains a parity-compatible endpoint when an integer point exists. Thus the feasibility test is complete and monotone.
